labelChirho: stumbling block, obstacle, cause of offense
descriptionChirho: Something that causes someone to stumble, trip, or fall into sin — used both for literal obstacles and metaphorically for moral/spiritual hindrances. The multilingual translations are consistent across both clusters: Spanish 'tropiezo' (stumbling/obstacle), Arabic 'ʿathra' (stumbling/trip), Korean '걸림/걸림돌/부딪침' (obstacle/stumbling stone/collision), Swahili 'kikwazo/kujikwaa' (obstacle/to stumble), Hindi 'ठोकर' (stumbling/kick). The two clusters differ only in case form (accusative/nominative vs genitive) with no semantic divergence; all Pauline uses refer metaphorically to causing spiritual offense.
